beats.say: A woodpecker slams its face into wood up to twenty times a second.
So I shrank myself down to bird size, to watch it up close.
The woodpecker. It can peck about twelve thousand times a day.
For years, people thought its head worked like a shock absorber.
Then high speed cameras caught it in the act. It doesn't.
Its head hits like a stiff hammer. Beak and brain stop together.
So why no concussion? Its brain is about seven hundred times smaller than ours.
Tiny brains take hits better. It would have to strike about twice as fast to get hurt.
And its tongue? It's so long, it wraps around its skull when it's not in use.
The tip has barbs, to hook bugs out of their holes.
Stiff tail feathers prop it up on the trunk, like a kickstand.
One kind, the acorn woodpecker, stuffs acorns into holes in a tree. One per hole.
A single tree can hold up to fifty thousand acorns.
Meanwhile, I can't even find my keys.
Would you want one drumming outside your window at six in the morning?
Twelve thousand head bangs a day, and its tongue lives wrapped around its skull.
Follow me. Next, another animal that shouldn't exist.
